findings.finding: The multi-project inbound fetch child scopes JQL fan-out and the truncation ceiling per project but does not address the three per-project enrichment passes the current fetcher runs (get_parent_map / get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map), each of which takes exactly one project key; fanning out the base JQL while leaving enrichment single-project silently drops inbound parent/comment/issuelink data for every project but one.
findings.location: Child decomposition — 'Multi-project inbound fetch'; vs src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:593-718 (_build_snapshot enrichment)
findings.suggested_fix: Have _build_snapshot iterate the configured project set for the enrichment step too — call get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map once per project and merge each result — and add the multi-project enrichment fidelity to the two-project fetch acceptance test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign the synchronous 'stamp in the same operation as the mapping write' half of parent AC7 to a specific child (extend c927's write path or add the missing store-compat-stamp child) with an AC asserting .store-compat.json is re-stamped in the same operation as a `bridge projects set/remove` mutation.
evidence: Parent AC7: '...store-compat test covers both, including the stamp updating in the SAME operation as the mapping write.'

Parent decomposition: 'Store-compat capability stamp — ... the bridge projects set/remove write path re-derives the stamp SYNCHRONOUSLY in the same operation as the mapping mutation (ensure sweeps are convergence backstops, not the trigger) ... test covers add (>1) and remove (<=1) transitions plus the synchronous-stamp property.'
Child 67f9 Approach: 'Registering the name here is inert on its own — nothing stamps it in this story ... The conditional stamp lands separately.'
Child 462d stamps only through the ensure unit, which the parent decomposition explicitly designates 'convergence backstops, not the trigger'.

Child c927 ACs cover set/list/remove, cross-surface parity, resolve_project, argument errors, absent/malformed, read/write tool registration, remove-unknown, replace-not-merge, and pinned help — but assert only that bindings.json and prev_snapshot.json are byte-identical after a mapping write and never mention .store-compat.json being (re-)stamped in the same operation.
findings.finding: Parent AC7's synchronous-stamp clause — 'including the stamp updating in the SAME operation as the mapping write' — is not covered by any sibling in the roster. The parent's child decomposition names a dedicated 'Store-compat capability stamp' child to deliver exactly this (the bridge-projects set/remove write path re-derives the stamp SYNCHRONOUSLY in the same operation as the mapping mutation, 'so no window exists where a multi-project store is un-stamped and an older binary un-gated'), but no such child exists among the 12 roster entries.
findings.location: child c927-0a68-4465-42a2 (owner of the bridge projects set/remove write path) and the missing 'Store-compat capability stamp' child
scenarios: An operator runs `bridge projects set` to add a second project; between the mapping write committing and the next ensure sweep, the store is multi-project but un-stamped, and an older binary is un-gated and can create duplicate issues in the wrong project — the exact window the parent AC7 clause exists to close.
The epic completion verifier checks parent AC7's same-operation clause and finds no child AC asserting the synchronous-stamp property; the epic cannot be marked complete.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the synchronous-stamp responsibility and its AC to child c927 (which owns the set/remove write path), or introduce the 'Store-compat capability stamp' child the parent decomposition names, with an AC asserting the stamp updates in the same operation as the mapping write (add >1 and remove <=1 transitions plus the no-window property).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion to child 1734 asserting get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map run once per configured project and that both projects' enrichment data appear in the merged snapshot.
evidence: Parent AC2: '...reconciler test asserts one JQL pair AND one enrichment pass (parent/comment/issuelink maps) per configured project, both projects' enrichment data present in the merged snapshot, and the recorded project on each created ticket.'

Parent decomposition (Multi-project inbound fetch): '...AND its three enrichment passes — get_parent_map / get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map called once per project, results merged into the shared snapshot keyed by issue (single-project enrichment would silently drop parent/comment/issuelink data for every project but one)...'

Child 1734 ACs enumerate: JQL pair per project; source project + repos recorded; per-project truncation ceiling; single-project identical query regression; zero-issue project does not fail — but no enrichment-pass or merged-enrichment-data assertion.
Child 1734 Approach discusses only the base JQL fan-out and snapshot union; it does not mention get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map at all.
findings.finding: Parent AC2's enrichment-fidelity half is not covered by child 1734's acceptance criteria. Parent AC2 requires 'one enrichment pass (parent/comment/issuelink maps) per configured project, both projects' enrichment data present in the merged snapshot', but child 1734 — the sole child delivering the two-project fetch criterion — has ACs only for JQL-pair count, source-project recording, per-project truncation, single-project regression, and zero-issue projects. None asserts the per-project enrichment passes or that both projects' enrichment data lands in the merged snapshot. This is partial coverage without the remainder being named.
scenarios: Two projects are configured; enrichment (parent/comment/issuelink maps) runs for only the first project, silently dropping parent/comment/issuelink data for the second — a defect the parent AC's enrichment assertion is designed to catch but which 1734's ACs would let pass green.
The epic completion verifier checks parent AC2's enrichment clause and finds no child AC asserting per-project enrichment or merged enrichment data.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend child 1734's ACs with an enrichment-fidelity criterion: a two-project reconciler test asserting one enrichment pass per project and both projects' parent/comment/issuelink data present in the merged snapshot keyed by issue.

findings.finding: Parent AC2 requires 'one enrichment pass (parent/comment/issuelink maps) is issued per configured project, with both projects' enrichment data present in the merged snapshot', but child 1734 — the sole child owning fetcher.py — covers only the JQL-search fan-out and never fans out the three enrichment passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to child 1734's Approach and ACs an explicit per-project enrichment fan-out (loop the three map calls over the configured project set, merging each into the shared snapshot) and an AC asserting both projects' parent/comment/issuelink data are present in the merged snapshot.

findings.finding: The parent decomposition's 'Store-compat capability stamp' child requires changing _store_compat_unit from 'blob absent' to a 'committed required_capabilities != desired set' check that covers BOTH the add-at-second-project AND remove-on-reverse transitions, with write_compat_record computing the capability list and a test covering BOTH transitions — but no child in the roster owns the reverse (de-stamp) transition or the write_compat_record list computation.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend child 462d's capability-stamp unit to compute the desired capability set from the mapping and re-write .store-compat.json whenever the committed set differs (covering both add and remove), and add its ACs for the reverse transition; correspondingly widen 67f9 or 462d to own the write_compat_record list computation in compat.py.

findings.finding: Parent AC2 requires that one enrichment pass (parent/comment/issuelink maps) is issued per configured project with both projects' enrichment data present in the merged snapshot, but child 1734 — the sibling the parent decomposition assigns this to ('Enrichment fidelity joins the two-project fetch acceptance test') — carries no acceptance criterion, approach note, or scope line covering enrichment fan-out. Its ACs cover only the JQL pair per project and the recorded project/repos. No other sibling covers per-project enrichment either.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend child 1734's Approach/Scope to fan get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map across every configured project (one call each per project, merged keyed by issue) and add an acceptance criterion asserting the per-project enrichment call count and both projects' enrichment data in the merged snapshot, matching parent AC2's wording.

findings.finding: Parent acceptance criterion 2 requires that 'one enrichment pass (parent/comment/issuelink maps) is issued per configured project, with both projects' enrichment data present in the merged snapshot' — but the multi-project inbound fetch child (1734) covers only the JQL-pair fan-out and source-project recording; its acceptance criteria say nothing about the three per-project enrichment passes. No sibling covers the enrichment remainder, so this half of AC2 is uncovered.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an acceptance criterion to child 1734 asserting one enrichment call per configured project for each of get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map with both projects' data merged into the snapshot, and add the enrichment merge site (fetcher._build_snapshot:577-685) to its scope; this also closes the G4 owned-by-none gap on the enrichment merge that both 1734 and a33c touch but neither owns.

findings.finding: The parent decomposition names a distinct 'Store-compat capability stamp' child whose defining behaviour is changing _store_compat_unit's check-then-act to re-stamp on divergence so it can BOTH add multi-project-bridge at a second project AND remove it on the reverse transition, 'test covers BOTH transitions.' No sibling in the roster owns the reverse (removal) transition. Child 462d only stamps (adds) the capability when the mapping holds more than one project; it never tests removal when a store drops back to one project. Child 67f9 only registers the capability name and tests fail-closed reads, not stamping. The reverse-transition behaviour is owned by NO sibling.
findings.suggested_fix: Either extend child 462d's stamp unit to compute required_capabilities from the mapping on every sweep (re-stamp when committed set != desired, covering removal) with a paired both-transitions AC, or add the missing standalone 'Store-compat capability stamp' child named in the parent decomposition with that behaviour and test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the atomicity/ordering mechanism binding the mapping write and the stamp re-derivation (e.g. both staged into ONE tickets-branch commit, or the stamp committed strictly before the mapping so a partial write never yields a multi-project mapping lacking its gating capability), so the 'no un-stamped window' property holds under crash/partial-write, not just in the happy path.
evidence: Plan: 'the bridge projects set/remove write path re-derives the stamp SYNCHRONOUSLY in the same operation as the mapping mutation ... so no window exists where a multi-project store is un-stamped'
compat.py write_compat_record and the mapping write are separate fsutil.atomic_write + git add/commit operations; nothing in the plan binds them into one atomic commit
init._store_compat_unit today writes and commits .store-compat.json as its own commit, separate from any mapping write
ABSENCE: the plan names the property (synchronous) and a test for it, but not the failure-case mechanism (what happens if the mapping write commits and the stamp write fails, or vice versa)
findings.finding: The store-compat stamp is claimed to leave 'no window' where a multi-project store is un-stamped, but projects.json (the mapping) and .store-compat.json (the stamp) are two distinct committed tickets-branch files; the plan states the no-window goal without specifying the atomicity/ordering mechanism (single commit, or stamp committed before/with the mapping) that actually guarantees it against a partial or crashed write.
findings.location: Approach / 'Store-compat capability stamp' child; AC7 'the stamp updating in the SAME operation as the mapping write'
scenarios: bridge projects set adds a second project: mapping commit succeeds, process crashes before the stamp commit -> a genuinely multi-project store with no multi-project-bridge stamp, and an older binary is un-gated (the exact failure the gate exists to prevent)
reverse ordering: stamp lands with >1 caps but the mapping write fails -> a single-project store incorrectly gated
findings.suggested_fix: State that bridge projects set/remove stages projects.json and .store-compat.json into a single atomic tickets-branch commit; if a single commit is not feasible, require the stamp (>1-cap) to be committed before the mapping mutation and removed after, so no committed multi-project mapping can exist without its gating stamp.
